structured_review.summary: The 2026 Orbit borrows the Orbit Pro's NMAX 2 frame and slimmer leading edge, fixing the old weak spots of lift and stability; testers crashed it repeatedly without a frontstall. Loops remain safe and predictable with light bar pressure in strong wind, but it is a twin-tip big air kite that does not like light wind.
pros: More lift and hangtime than previous Orbits
Very stable; hard to frontstall even after crashes
Safe, predictable kiteloops that catch reliably
Light bar pressure that stays manageable when overpowered
Orbit Pro materials at the standard Orbit price
cons: Big air focus; little versatility for foil or waves
structured_review.best_for: Twin-tip riders who want to jump high and learn kiteloops in strong wind.
structured_review.not_for: Light-wind riders or anyone wanting a multi-discipline kite.
structured_review.rec_blurb: Orbit Pro DNA at the Orbit price: steadier, floatier, still a loop machine.
